verdict_reason: Your hypothesis is wrong for this one. Only 3 of the 30 sampled tiles are actually at the Temple of Literature (one photographer, ids 4318276433 / 4318284825 / 4319010702 - Khue Van Cac is unmistakable in the third). One tile (5742954673) is not even in Hanoi: it is a floating fish-farm village in front of limestone karst, i.e. the Ha Long / Cat Ba coast, ~150 km away. The remaining ~22 tiles are a single photographer's contiguous batch (8599844525-8600946014) documenting a HUY PHONG JSC cyclo tour that never goes near Van Mieu: the Hanoi Opera House appears twice, and legible street evidence puts the ride squarely in Hoan Kiem's French Quarter - the street plate 'PHO LY DAO THANH', 'CLUB OPERA' at 59 Ly Thai To, the Gucci canopy reading 'LY THAI TO', the EMIC electrical-meter works whose address was 10 Tran Nguyen Han, and Sentinel Place at 41A Ly Thai To (corner of Tran Nguyen Han). Van Mieu is ~2.5 km west of all of that. So the pin is a place-picker centroid catching whole Hanoi trips, not a landmark pile.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Tourist group on a brick-paved axial path through a lawned courtyard hung with red lanterns and festival banners, stone lanterns and clipped shrubs; at the end of the axis a two-tier red timber pavilion with a circular window on white stone piers, i.e. Khue Van Cac seen down the courtyard, the same building photographed close-up in 4319010702 by the same uploader.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Lacquered and gilded shrine cabinet with a dragon-carved throne inside, flanked by a red column bearing a vertical Han couplet ending '...百王之標準' ('the standard of a hundred kings'), Confucian panegyric language. Interior of a Confucian shrine hall and same photographer/session as the two confirmed Van Mieu frames, but no view of the building exterior.

photos.place: Khue Van Cac, Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: The two-storey red timber pavilion on two carved white stone piers, upturned dragon-crested roof, circular sunburst window ('Khue' star) on each face, red lanterns hung from the eaves, and the third-courtyard gate with its tiled roof visible through the archway. This is Khue Van Cac, the Temple of Literature's emblematic pavilion.

Bronze dragon writhing up the corner of a stone/bronze incense burner packed with spent red joss sticks, on large flagstone paving, with a gilt-carved wooden panel behind. A Vietnamese temple courtyard - but nothing distinguishes which temple, so I will not name one.

photos.place: Cat Ba / Ha Long Bay floating village, Vietnam
photos.evidence: A cluster of dozens of floating timber houses and fish-farm pens on flat grey water in front of two steep, jungle-topped limestone karst hills, palm fronds in the foreground implying an elevated shore viewpoint. This is the Ha Long / Lan Ha / Cat Ba karst coast (Cai Beo-type floating village), definitively not Hanoi and definitively not the Temple of Literature.

Timber-panelled hall laid out for a traditional-music demonstration: dan t'rung bamboo xylophone, dan tranh zither, a rank of large bamboo tubes on a red-carpeted platform, painted fans and souvenir scrolls for sale on the walls. A tourist performance room (Van Mieu's Thai Hoc house does host these) but there is no sign, ticket or exterior to confirm the venue.

Narrow two-way street of 3-4 storey shophouses with continuous awnings, dense goods displays and a magazine/confectionery stall on the pavement, vertical neon signs; a green fascia at right is only partly legible. Old-Quarter fabric, but no street plate or resolvable business name.

Wide, double tree-lined avenue with old-style lamp standards and a green park strip on the left, light traffic, a manhole in a smooth asphalt carriageway. This is the Ba Dinh / French-Quarter boulevard type (Dien Bien Phu, Hoang Dieu, Tran Phu, Phan Dinh Phung all look like this) with no readable plate or building to choose between them.

photos.place: Hanoi Opera House (Nha hat Lon Ha Noi), Hanoi
photos.evidence: The ochre-and-white neoclassical opera house with its slate dome, rusticated ground floor, balustraded balcony and Ionic loggia, behind the black iron fence on its yellow plinth wall, national flag flying; shot from the roadway with the concrete bollard rail in front.

Row of HUY PHONG JSC tour cyclos (numbered 22, 44) with drivers in pale blue uniforms waiting in front of an ornate black iron fence on a grey plinth, mature street trees behind. Cross-photo evidence from the same batch (Ly Thai To, Tran Nguyen Han, Opera House) puts the staging point in Hoan Kiem's French Quarter, but this frame alone shows no plate or nameable building.

Pavement banh-mi/tea stall under a huge street tree in front of a colonial building with arched first-floor windows; the utility kiosk in the middle of the frame is lettered 'CONG TY THIET BI DO DIEN EMIC', and a red banner above marks a 30-year anniversary. EMIC (Cong ty Thiet bi Do dien EMIC) had its works and head office at 10 Tran Nguyen Han, Hoan Kiem - confirmed by search - and Tran Nguyen Han also fits the rest of this cyclo route (Sentinel Place, one frame later, is on the Ly Thai To/Tran Nguyen Han corner).

Pavement rice canteen: red vertical 'COM' signs, plastic stools and steel tables crowded with office workers, a yellow banner overhead whose only resolvable word is '...LINH', motorbikes and a cyclo on the kerb. Old-Quarter street eatery with no street plate visible.

Two-storey French colonial villa/office with tall shuttered casements and a national flag, behind a low balustraded wall and iron gate; large grey electrical cabinet on the pavement, tangle of overhead cables. The blue-and-white sign on the gatepost resolves only to a 'CAM DO' (no parking) notice, so the street cannot be named.

French colonial villa with a steep tiled roof and dormer behind a rubble-stone wall topped with iron railings, heavily treed street, red-and-white no-parking posts. Classic Hanoi French-Quarter/Ba Dinh villa street; no plate or house number legible.

Pale-yellow modern colonial-style commercial block with a GUCCI flagship at ground level and a glazed canopy over the lobby entrance; the lettering on the canopy fascia reads 'LY THAI TO' at full resolution. That places the frame on Ly Thai To street (the Opera Business Centre / Gucci frontage).

Cyclos parked and being turned on a tree-lined street beside a small formal park with green benches, hedge-edged lawn and an ornate wrought-iron lamp standard; a city bus passes behind. Consistent with the Ly Thai To / Ngo Quyen / Tran Nguyen Han park block that this cyclo tour demonstrably rides through, but the park has no visible nameplate or fountain to identify it.

Two Western tourists seated in HUY PHONG JSC cyclos (No. 13) with drivers standing by, in front of an ornate black iron fence and a cream shuttered colonial building. Same staging point as 8599844969/8599847199; no plate or nameable landmark in frame.

Line of HUY PHONG JSC cyclos (Nos. 86, 92) with tourists aboard on a paved forecourt in front of the same scrollwork iron fence. Batch context places it in the French Quarter; nothing in the frame names the spot.

Cyclos and motorbikes in a narrow street of 5-6 storey buildings; a restaurant fascia in red letters is only partly resolvable ('...TRUNG', with a smaller 'Dac san' line) and a neighbouring sign ends '...HOI'. Dense mixed-height Old-Quarter/edge-of-Old-Quarter street with no readable street plate.

View forward from a cyclo over the driver's shoulder (plate 29XL 0108) along a tree-lined street with a formal park, ornate lamp posts and a pedestrian-crossing sign to the right. Same block as 8599846973; no nameplate visible.

photos.place: Sentinel Place, 41A Ly Thai To, Hanoi
photos.evidence: Modern glass-and-stone office building with cantilevered glass canopies; the entrance fascia lettering reads as 'Sentinel Place', a blue tenant sign above ends in '...solutions', and a red board offers 'COMMERCIAL SPACE FOR LEASE / CHO THUE THUONG MAI 0948 000 468'. Search confirms Sentinel Place is 41A Ly Thai To on the Tran Nguyen Han corner, which is exactly where this cyclo batch's other confirmed frames sit.

Cyclo (plate 29XL 0139) riding up a shophouse street; the left-hand fascia reads 'BANH CUON NONG - GIO CHA' over an open food shop, with a Soviet-era stair-access block above and a Vinaphone/mobile sign further along. Old-Quarter commerce but the shop name is generic and no street plate is visible.

Busy intersection looking at a large cream institutional building with pilasters, red national flags and a monumental iron gate between piers, big street trees. A French-Quarter ministry/agency compound, but no name board, plate or house number is readable.

Cyclos riding away down a heavily treed street; right side has a no-parking roundel, a pedestrian-crossing sign, an electrical cabinet and a red shop banner with unresolvable text; left side a modern rendered building. No street plate.

Two rows of parked scooters on a wide brick pavement against a blue corrugated construction hoarding, under a big tree; a blue 'P' parking sign is present but its upper and lower text lines are illegible even at 12x, and a small blue plate on the pole cannot be read.

Colonial villa entrance with a gilt-on-black hanging sign reading 'CLUB OPERA' under a green porch, a wall plaque numbered '59A', and an OMEGA boutique window immediately right. Search confirms Club Opera is at 59 Ly Thai To, Trang Tien, Hoan Kiem.

Corner building housing an OMEGA boutique with a street clock; on the pole at left the blue street plate reads 'PHO LY DAO THANH' clearly at 12x, alongside a blue 'P' sign and a Vietnam-Telecom board. Ly Dao Thanh is the short Hoan Kiem street off Ly Thai To, matching the Club Opera / Omega frontage seen in 8600945550.

Colonial commercial block with a HUGO BOSS store and a gold-lettered boutique next to it, an enormous banyan with aerial roots on the pavement, a white taxi passing, ornate lamp standard. The luxury-boutique frontage and building type match the Ly Thai To / Opera Business Centre run that this batch documents, but the blue street plate nailed to the tree is unreadable at full resolution, so the street is inferred from the neighbouring frames rather than read.

photos.place: Hanoi Opera House (Nha hat Lon Ha Noi), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Motorbike passing in front of the same ochre-and-white opera house - balustraded parapet, arched and pedimented windows, slate dome behind - seen through the palms and black iron fence on its yellow plinth wall, with the concrete-post rail along the kerb.
